ant.definition: A small insect with six legs that lives in organised groups.
ant.exampleUsage: The ant carried material toward its colony's nest.

bee.definition: An insect of a group that commonly gathers pollen and nectar; only some bees make substantial honey stores.
bee.exampleUsage: The bee gathered pollen from the flower.

butterfly.definition: An insect of the butterfly group, with scaled wings in its adult stage.
butterfly.exampleUsage: The butterfly moved between the flowers.

ladybug.definition: A beetle of the ladybird family, many species of which have spotted wing covers.
ladybug.exampleUsage: The ladybug walked across a leaf beside the aphids.

dragonfly.definition: A flying insect with a long body and two pairs of wings.
dragonfly.exampleUsage: The dragonfly flew above the pond.

grasshopper.definition: A jumping insect with long back legs that eats plants.
grasshopper.exampleUsage: The grasshopper jumped using its long back legs.

beetle.definition: An insect whose hardened front wings cover the flight wings when at rest.
beetle.exampleUsage: The beetle opened its hardened wing covers before flight.

fly.definition: An insect with one pair of wings and large eyes.
fly.exampleUsage: The fly landed briefly on the surface.

mosquito.definition: A fly of the mosquito family; females of many species take blood meals, while feeding behavior varies by species.
mosquito.exampleUsage: The mosquito rested on the vegetation near the pond.

cricket.exampleUsage: The cricket chirped from the grass.
cricket.definition: An insect known for the chirping sound made by its wings.

wing.definition: A body structure used in insect flight, where present in the species or life stage.
wing.exampleUsage: The insect extended one wing before taking flight.

antenna.definition: One of the paired sensory appendages on an insect’s head.
antenna.exampleUsage: The insect moved an antenna while exploring the surface.

leg.definition: One of an adult insect’s six walking appendages, attached to its thorax.
leg.exampleUsage: The insect placed one leg on the leaf's edge.

thorax.definition: The middle region of the body of an arthropod between the head and the abdomen.
thorax.exampleUsage: The adult insect's six legs attach to its thorax.

abdomen.definition: The rear body region of an insect, behind the thorax.
abdomen.exampleUsage: The abdomen is behind the thorax in the reference.

head.definition: The front body region of an insect, bearing sensory organs and mouthparts.
head.exampleUsage: The insect's head carries sensory organs and mouthparts.

eye.definition: A sensory organ used for vision, often compound in adult insects.
eye.exampleUsage: The enlarged reference shows the insect's compound eye.

mandible.definition: One of the paired insect mouthparts used for biting or manipulating material.
mandible.exampleUsage: The insect used a mandible to manipulate plant material.

stinger.definition: A sharp organ of offense or defense (as of a wasp or stingray or scorpion) often connected with a poison gland.
stinger.exampleUsage: The anatomical reference shows the wasp's stinger.

proboscis.definition: An elongated mouthpart used by certain insects to take in food or liquids.
proboscis.exampleUsage: The butterfly uncoiled its proboscis to take in liquid.

hive.definition: A structure in which a colony of bees lives.
hive.exampleUsage: The managed hive houses a colony of bees.

anthill.definition: A mound of earth made by ants as they dig their nest.
anthill.exampleUsage: The anthill rose above the surrounding soil.

web.definition: A network of silk threads made by a spider.
web.exampleUsage: The spider waited beside its silk web.

cocoon.definition: A protective silk covering made by some insects during development.
cocoon.exampleUsage: The moth's pupa developed inside a silk cocoon.

nest.definition: A structure or place used by an animal for shelter or raising young.
nest.exampleUsage: The ants carried material toward the nest entrance.

burrow.definition: A hole or tunnel made by an animal for shelter.
burrow.exampleUsage: The comparison display shows an animal's underground burrow.

leaf.definition: A flat green part of a plant that uses light to make food.
leaf.exampleUsage: The caterpillar fed along the edge of a leaf.

bark.definition: The rough outer covering of a tree trunk.
bark.exampleUsage: The insect rested on the tree's bark.

soil.definition: Material in the top layer of the surface of the earth in which plants can grow (especially with reference to its quality or use).
soil.exampleUsage: The earthworm moved through the moist soil.

pond-surface.definition: The topmost layer of a pond is the boundary where its water meets the air.
pond-surface.exampleUsage: The insect rested on the pond surface where water meets air.

larva.definition: An immature insect stage in complete metamorphosis, generally unlike the adult form.
larva.exampleUsage: The beetle larva fed before entering its pupal stage.

caterpillar.definition: A young insect that looks like a worm before becoming a butterfly or moth.
caterpillar.exampleUsage: The caterpillar grew on its host plant.

pupa.definition: An insect in the inactive stage of development (when it is not feeding) intermediate between larva and adult.
pupa.exampleUsage: The pupa developed into an adult without feeding during the pupal stage.

chrysalis.definition: The pupal stage of a butterfly, distinct from a surrounding silk cocoon.
chrysalis.exampleUsage: The butterfly emerged from the chrysalis.

metamorphosis.definition: Developmental changes between immature and adult stages, complete or incomplete depending on the insect.
metamorphosis.exampleUsage: The guide compared complete and incomplete metamorphosis.

molt.definition: Periodic shedding of the cuticle in arthropods or the outer skin in reptiles.
molt.exampleUsage: The insect's molt involved shedding its old outer covering.

nymph.definition: An immature stage in insects with incomplete metamorphosis, generally resembling the adult but not fully developed.
nymph.exampleUsage: The grasshopper nymph grew through successive molts.

adult.exampleUsage: The adult insect had completed its immature developmental stages.
adult.definition: An insect in its mature life stage.

swarm.definition: A gathered or moving group of insects.
swarm.exampleUsage: A swarm of insects gathered above the vegetation.

pollinate.definition: To transfer pollen to the receptive part of a flower, a process that can enable fertilization.
pollinate.exampleUsage: Insects can pollinate flowers by transferring pollen.

sting.definition: To puncture with a stinger and potentially introduce venom.
sting.exampleUsage: Some wasps can sting when disturbed.

crawl.definition: To move forward close to the ground on hands, knees, or legs.
crawl.exampleUsage: The small insects crawl across the leaf surface.

buzz.definition: To produce the humming sound associated with the movement of some insects’ wings.
buzz.exampleUsage: The flying insects buzz near the flowers.

dig.definition: To turn up, loosen, or remove earth.
dig.exampleUsage: The ants dig passages through the soil.

spin.definition: To produce silk threads or structures in the stated organism.
spin.exampleUsage: Some larvae spin silk to form a protective covering.

camouflage.definition: Appearance or behavior that helps an organism blend with its surroundings.
camouflage.exampleUsage: The insect's camouflage made it difficult to see against the twig.

migrate.exampleUsage: Some insect species migrate between regions.

hibernate.definition: To spend the winter in a state of greatly reduced activity.
hibernate.exampleUsage: The guide explained that some insects hibernate during cold periods.

earthworm.definition: Terrestrial worm that burrows into and helps aerate soil.
earthworm.exampleUsage: The earthworm burrowed through moist soil.

snail.definition: A small slow-moving animal with a spiral shell.
snail.exampleUsage: The snail moved slowly with its shell on its back.

slug.definition: A slow-moving animal similar to a snail but without an external shell.
slug.exampleUsage: The slug crossed the damp ground without an external shell.

centipede.definition: A predatory many-segmented arthropod with one pair of legs per body segment; it is not an insect.
centipede.exampleUsage: The centipede moved with one pair of legs on each body segment.

millipede.definition: A many-segmented arthropod with two pairs of legs on most apparent body segments; it is not an insect.
millipede.exampleUsage: The millipede has two leg pairs on most apparent body segments.

aphid.definition: Any of various small plant-sucking insects.
aphid.exampleUsage: The aphid fed on the plant's sap.

praying-mantis.definition: A predatory insect with a long body and large front legs held in a folded position that resembles hands in prayer.
praying-mantis.exampleUsage: The praying mantis waited motionless on a leaf.

firefly.definition: A beetle of the firefly family, many species of which produce light through bioluminescence.
firefly.exampleUsage: The firefly produced light during the observed display.

moth.definition: An insect commonly called moth, belonging to the same broad order as butterflies; many species are active at night, but not all.
moth.exampleUsage: The moth rested on the shaded tree trunk.

wasp.definition: An insect commonly called wasp, belonging to a group including social and solitary species.
wasp.exampleUsage: The wasp visited the flower beside the path.
